subject: mathematics
question_text: If x = 2 sin θ/(1 + cos θ + sin θ), find the value of (1 − cos θ + sin θ)/(1 + sin θ).

mark_split.label: Multiply by 1 + cos θ + sin θ

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 23, book p.86. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards the multiplication and the difference-of-two-squares grouping first and the cancellation that produces x second. The route here uses no half-angle substitution on purpose: tan(θ/2) would add the extra condition cos θ ≠ −1, and the difference-of-two-squares route needs only the two conditions the question already carries. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations holds two of those ten slots. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Checked numerically at θ = 50°, 130°, 240° and 310°: x and the asked expression agree to ten decimal places at every one (0.6360297657, 1.3639702343, 4.7320508076 and −1.7474774195).

recall_prompt: Say what you would multiply this expression by, and say what value it comes out to.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply by 1 + cos θ + sin θ
steps.margin_note: First mark. Group the numerator as (1 + sin θ) − cos θ so that the multiplier is (1 + sin θ) + cos θ. Both conditions written here are the ones the two given fractions already need.
steps.memory_tip: Group as (1 + sin θ) − cos θ and (1 + sin θ) + cos θ. Their product is (1 + sin θ)² − cos²θ.
lines: x is given, so 1 + cos θ + sin θ ≠ 0.
The asked expression needs 1 + sin θ ≠ 0.
Multiply its top and bottom by
Nr = (1 + sin θ − cos θ)(1 + sin θ + cos θ)

recall.must_convey: That the top and bottom are multiplied by (1 + cos θ + sin θ), and the numerator becomes 2 sin θ (1 + sin θ) by the difference of two squares.
accept: multiply top and bottom by one plus cos theta plus sin theta
group as one plus sin theta minus cos theta and one plus sin theta plus cos theta to get a difference of two squares
the numerator becomes two sin theta into one plus sin theta
top and bottom ni one plus cos theta plus sin theta tho multiply chestam
use a squared minus b squared with a as one plus sin theta

steps.why: Grouping the numerator as (1 + sin θ) − cos θ and the multiplier as (1 + sin θ) + cos θ makes them a difference of two squares, and cos²θ then becomes 1 − sin²θ. That single grouping is the whole question.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only the numerator by (1 + cos θ + sin θ).
Writing cos²θ as 1 + sin²θ instead of 1 − sin²θ.

steps.label: Cancel and read off x
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The factor 1 + sin θ is on the top and the bottom and is not 0, so it cancels. What is left is the given expression for x.
steps.memory_tip: After the multiplication the factor (1 + sin θ) cancels, and what remains is exactly the given expression for x.
lines: Dr = (1 + sin θ)(1 + cos θ + sin θ)
Since 1 + sin θ ≠ 0 it cancels, leaving
2 sin θ/(1 + cos θ + sin θ), which is x.

lines.text: ∴ (1 − cos θ + sin θ)/(1 + sin θ) = x

recall.must_convey: That 1 + sin θ cancels and the remaining expression is the given x, so the value is x.
accept: one plus sin theta cancels and what is left is two sin theta over one plus cos theta plus sin theta which is x
after cancelling you get back the given expression so the answer is x
one plus sin theta cancel avutundi, answer x

steps.why: The factor 1 + sin θ appears on the top and the bottom and cancels, because the question already needs it to be non-zero for the expression to exist. What is left is exactly the given expression for x, so the value asked for is x itself.
common_mistakes: Cancelling 1 + sin θ without saying that it is not 0.
Leaving the answer in θ when the question asks for a value in terms of x.
